chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: Hollywood Barn, the Plantation Club gunmen, and breaking with Dancer
summary: The band played a gay club and a gangster's Plantation Club, where gunmen turned them away because Dancer owed money; they finally gave him up.

bands.name: Earl Dancer and his Harlem Gentlemen

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now what happens then next with this band?
With Earl's band? Well we played all over, places like in Hollywood, there was a big place out there for homosexuals called the 'Hollywood Barn'.

Yes, the whole chorus line was men. And we played there for a long time. They did a lot of business. It was quite a business. And we played other places but we, we played some big gangster's place out there.

I remember this, we were playing there for a full week and we went to work, we went to go, to work that Saturday night the following Monday after and we hadn't been paid. But as soon as we got to the door, there were six guys standing out there with machine guns and turned us right around and made us go back to Los Angeles. No work because Earl had gambled all our money and had ran into some kind of trouble with the gangster leader. So he didn't want us back.
This was at a place called 'The Plantation Club'. They didn't want us back and they didn't want to see

So they just met us right on the doorway with machineguns. and told us to get the hell out of there. So we ended up with no money again. So that was about I think the last time that we worked for Earl because we decided then that we were never going to get anywhere. Because this had been going on for a long time.

A lot of times I as I sat in the club, where we lived upstairs in the hotel, the Dunbar Hotel, sometimes I'd get through work and go home and can't get in the door. They'd got a thing in my door because I couldn't pay my rent. My little dog was in there starving and they still wouldn't even open my door because Earl had goofed up our money, you see, in Club Ebony and this.
He would take the money and he would go all the way out to Hollywood and get in a poker game and....
That was too bad since it was a good band.
It was a good band, yes.
Earl Dancer and his Harlem Gentlemen. (LAUGHTER).
Who was the singer with this band? Did you have anybody?
Let's see. We had various singers.
No, we had mostly girls, but we didn't have any, nobody in the band sang. But we did have a lot of girls that were hired to sing. So we had to give up on Earl.
